previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, chronic aspiration, alcohol dependence, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for evaluation of leukocytosis (WBC 19.1) detected during a post-hospitalization clinic visit. He was asymptomatic with stable vital signs and no clinical signs of infection. Workup including blood, urine, and stool cultures was negative. Chest imaging showed stable interstitial opacities without new consolidation. The elevated white count was attributed to ongoing aspiration pneumonitis rather than active infection, and antibiotics were withheld given recent completion of a course. Hyponatremia improved with fluid restriction, and a new right PICC line was placed for potential future access. The patient remained clinically stable, and goals of care were reaffirmed: DNR/DNI status, continued oral feeding despite aspiration risk, and preference for hospitalization only with clear clinical decompensation. He was discharged to extended care with follow-up instructions and unchanged home medications.
